$comment: In-app help centre articles: versioned content (bump `version` and `updatedOn` on every change), localised per locale. `contexts` are app paths the article is linked from. `features` are the capabilities of the permission map (packages/core/src/capabilities.ts) the article covers and `permissions` the permissions it describes: a reader sees the article only with all of them, with each feature on for the workspace; `countries` limits it to workspaces with a legal entity in one of them. Only the general articles (signing in, accounts: GENERAL_HELP_SLUGS) have no feature. Fictional examples only.

en-GB.title: Getting started with your workspace
en-GB.summary: Set up your organisation, invite your team and turn on multi-factor authentication.
body: Your workspace lives in the home region you chose at sign-up. All of your people data, files and backups stay in that region.
Start with Settings → Organisation to add your legal entities, locations and departments. Then add people one by one from People, or import a spreadsheet from Imports.
Admins must turn on multi-factor authentication before they can use the app. Open Security to add an authenticator app or a passkey.

en-GB.title: Adding and importing people
en-GB.summary: Create employee records, schedule future-dated changes and bulk import from CSV or Excel.
body: Choose People → Add person to create a record. Changes can be dated in the future: they take effect automatically on their date and the full history is kept.
To add many people at once, download the template from Imports, fill it in and upload it. You see a validation preview before anything is saved, and large files run in the background with progress.
Your bill is based on the number of active employees. Leavers stop counting from their leaving date.

en-GB.title: Requesting and approving time off
en-GB.summary: Book holiday, see your balance and how approvals work.
body: Open Time off and choose Request time off. Your available balance is shown before you send the request, including public holidays where your policy deducts them.
Your manager is notified and can approve or decline from Approvals. You get a notification either way.
Statutory minimums come from the jurisdiction rules for your country, each with its official source.

en-GB.title: Rotas, clocking in and timesheets
en-GB.summary: Publish shifts, clock in on your phone or a kiosk, and approve timesheets.
body: Managers build the rota for the week and publish it. Everyone affected is notified.
Clock in from Clock on your phone, even without a signal: punches are queued on your device and sent when you are back online.
At the end of the week, submit your timesheet. Your manager approves it and payroll can export the approved hours.

en-GB.title: Contacting Thapsus-HR support
en-GB.summary: Raise a ticket, choose a priority and see our response times for your plan.
body: Open Support and choose New ticket. Describe what happened and attach a screenshot if it helps. Tickets are stored in your workspace's home region.
Pick the priority that matches the impact: urgent means the service is unusable for your company. Our first-response and resolution targets depend on your plan and are shown on each ticket.
Our support team can read what you send in a ticket. They cannot see anything else in your workspace unless an admin grants time-limited support access from Settings, and every access is logged.

en-GB.title: Plans, billing and cancelling
en-GB.summary: How the free trial, monthly and annual terms, upgrades, downgrades and cancellation work.
body: Every workspace starts with a free trial. Choose a plan, a monthly rolling or annual term and your billing currency from Billing. Prices depend on your number of active employees.
Upgrades take effect straight away and you pay only the difference for the rest of the period. Downgrades and switching from annual to monthly take effect at the end of the period you have paid for.

You can cancel at any time. Cancelling takes effect at the end of the billing period after your notice period; you keep full access until then and can reactivate before it ends. VAT or sales tax is added where it applies.

en-GB.title: Sign-in security, SSO and passkeys
en-GB.summary: Two-step verification, forgotten passwords, single sign-on and verified domains.
body: New workspaces require two-step verification for everyone: the first time you sign in, set up an authenticator app or a passkey. Your admins can turn this off for non-admin roles on the sign-in policy screen; admins always need it.

Forgot your password? Choose “Forgot your password?” on the sign-in page. If you have an account, we email you a link that works once for 30 minutes. It does not sign you in, and you still use your second factor afterwards.

To use single sign-on, verify your email domain in Settings and connect your identity provider with SAML 2.0 or OpenID Connect. You can then require SSO for everyone. The first SSO sign-in links your account to your identity provider account.
Sessions end after a period of inactivity and after a maximum length that your admins choose. Admin sessions end sooner: after 15 idle minutes and 8 hours at most.

en-GB.title: Who can reset passwords and two-step verification
en-GB.summary: What you can do yourself, what an admin can do for you, and who that admin can be.
body: You can always reset your own password: choose “Forgot your password?” on the sign-in page and follow the emailed link. It works once for 30 minutes and signs you out everywhere. Your two-step verification stays as it is.
If you signed in with an emailed link, you can set a new password on your Security page without your old one for the next few minutes.

An admin can, from Settings → Users and access → the person: sign them out everywhere, email them a password reset link (valid for 24 hours), reset a lost authenticator after confirming who they are, or unlink a replaced single sign-on account. The admin never sees or sets the password.

Who that admin can be: someone whose company-wide role includes managing settings and every permission the person has. So an owner can help anyone, but nobody can help someone with more access than they have, and nobody can do it for themselves. They confirm it is them first.
Every reset is recorded in the audit log, and the person is told by email. If you did not expect such an email, contact your admin straight away.
Thapsus-HR staff cannot reset your password or two-step verification.

en-GB.title: Giving Thapsus-HR support temporary access
en-GB.summary: Grant, limit and revoke support access to your workspace data.
body: Sometimes support needs to look at a record to fix a problem. Only an admin can allow this, for one named support person, for up to 30 days, as read-only or read and write.
Every time support opens your data it is written to your audit log and to our staff audit trail. You can revoke access at any time and it stops immediately.

en-GB.title: Viewing your payslips
en-GB.summary: Find your payslips and end-of-year certificates, and know when a new one arrives.

Your pay is calculated by your company's payroll provider. If something looks wrong, ask HR: open Help → Contact HR and say which payslip you mean.

en-GB.title: Signing documents
en-GB.summary: Read and sign the documents HR sends you, such as your contract.
body: When HR asks you to sign something, a task appears in your Inbox and you get a notification. Both open the document.
Read the document, then type your full name and confirm that you agree to sign electronically. The date and time of your signature are recorded with it.
Signed documents stay in Documents, where you can open them at any time.

Your job, pay and contract are changed by HR. If something is out of date, open Help → Contact HR.

en-GB.title: Notifications and what to do with them
en-GB.summary: Open what a notification is about, mark it read and choose how you are told.
body: The bell in the top bar shows how many notifications you have not read. Open it to see the latest ones.
Each notification opens the thing it is about: a request to approve, a task, your time off or a document to sign. Opening one marks it read. Mark all as read clears the rest.
Open My profile → Notifications to choose which kinds reach you by email or as a push notification on this device. You always see them in the app.

en-GB.title: Asking HR a question

en-GB.title: Signing in and your account
en-GB.summary: Sign in, use two-step verification, see where you are signed in and choose your language and theme.
body: Sign in with your work email and password, or with single sign-on if your organisation uses it. Your workspace may ask for a second step: a code from an authenticator app or a passkey on this device.
Open Security to change your password, add or remove a passkey, set up a new authenticator app and see where you are signed in. You can sign out of every other device from there.
The account menu in the top bar sets your language and the light or dark theme, and signs you out.
Forgot your password? Choose “Forgot your password?” on the sign-in page and follow the emailed link.

en-GB.title: Asking Ask HR about company policies
en-GB.summary: Ask a question about your company’s own policies and see where each answer comes from.
body: Open Help → Ask HR and type a question about a company policy, such as how to book time off for a medical appointment. Ask HR answers only from the policy documents your HR team has chosen, and lists the passages it used.
Answers are written by an AI model. Check the cited policy before you rely on an answer, and ask your HR team when something is unclear.
Ask HR declines questions about colleagues’ personal matters, and it never makes or recommends decisions about anyone’s employment.

en-GB.title: Your logo and accent colour
en-GB.summary: Show your logo in the navigation and use your own accent colour for links and buttons.
body: Open Settings → Branding and enter your accent colour as a six-digit hex value, for example #1F3A8A. You can choose a different colour for dark mode.
To keep the app readable for everyone, a colour is saved only when it meets WCAG 2.2 AA contrast on every background in light and dark mode. If it does not, you see which pairs fall short.
Upload a PNG, JPEG or WebP logo of up to 512 KB. It is stored in your home region.
People who can view the workspace settings see Branding read-only; admins who manage the workspace settings change it.

en-GB.title: Form I-9 records
en-GB.summary: Track Section 1, Section 2 and reverification for people employed in the United States.
body: Open Compliance → Form I-9 to see each person employed by a US entity, with the dates Section 1 and Section 2 were completed, any reverification due and how long the form must be kept.
The deadlines shown come from the US rules pack, each with its official source, so they follow the rules when the rules change.
People who may record compliance information choose Update to enter the dates. Everyone else with access to Compliance sees the list read-only.

The check methods, the evidence each one needs and any follow-up dates come from the UK rules pack, each with its official source.
People who may record compliance information choose Record check, and can attach the evidence to the person’s documents. Everyone else with access to Compliance sees the list read-only.

en-GB.title: Equipment, accounts and leavers’ access
en-GB.summary: Issue equipment, record returns and connect your directory: the IT admin’s work.
body: IT admins keep the register under IT → Equipment: they add equipment, issue it to a person, who confirms they received it, and record each return with the checklist for its type.

Ordering a laptop, phone or site access card for a starter, removing a leaver’s system and building access, and recording what a leaver hands back are tasks in the IT admins’ inbox. While no one holds the IT admin role, they go to the role chosen in Settings → Workflow templates.

Under IT → Integrations, connect Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace to create and remove accounts when people join and leave. Settings → User provisioning (SCIM) gives your identity provider a token to provision sign-ins.
HR admins see the register read-only, so they can check what a leaver still holds. IT admins never see pay, contracts or sensitive records.
